question: Does Y035's parity-restricted repair advantage survive when true stable subgroups are key-specific latent SHA256 classes unrelated to parity?
hypothesis: A prewired parity-correction mechanism may not generalize when target drift groups are determined by a different hidden assignment, despite equal memory and feedback budget.
domain: 7 live/9 dormant observed key/value associations among 16 motifs, 12 episodes, SHA256-keyed Y033/Y030 active-key schedule. STABLE unchanged. HIDDEN_SWITCH at episode6 each key target changes by +1 if SHA256('Y036/'+seed+'/'+key) first-byte parity is0, otherwise +2 modulo4. The hidden subgroup hash is evaluator-only; policies never see its membership or formula.
arms: baseline: observed live association updates plus nine-slot dormant memory, no correction
global: detect a shared nonzero delta from live overlaps and correct every dormant value by the delta
prewired_parity: identical feedback, but apply detected shared delta only to dormant keys whose visible numeric parity matches all current agreeing live overlap cues
primary: Per heldout STABLE and HIDDEN_SWITCH post episode7..11 correct, dormant recall, total cache writes, extra correction mutations, per-seed true hidden-vs-parity misalignment. PARITY_GENERALIZES iff parity arm beats BOTH baseline and global after switch without stable degradation. FALSE_GROUP_PRIOR iff global or parity worse than baseline under switch. OTHERWISE_MIXED otherwise. No post-result thresholds.
safeguards: Three arms share exactly same 7+9 storage and observed-only label feedback after prediction, all active sets/evictions fixed, no target lookup before prediction, no additional oracle or capacity. Eight unique SHA256 signatures, deterministic repeat, immutable first-use artifact and full test regression. Negative results retained and no accepted-ref mutations.
claim_limit: Synthetic hidden-group memory repair falsification; not causal claims about neurons or general embodied intelligence.
